narrative:
The model estimates a 79% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system has learned from many similar employee profiles.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this prediction were your overall years of experience, whether you have received other job offers recently, and how long you have been with this organization. 

Your total professional experience of 6–10 years was the strongest driver pushing the prediction toward leaving. While many employees predicted to stay have shorter experience (50% have only 1–5 years), the model sees mid-level experience like yours as often linked to higher turnover as people look for the next step in their career. 

Having received other job opportunities was the second most important factor and also increased the likelihood of leaving. This suggests the model recognizes that external options can make staying less attractive.

Your relatively short time in your current role (1–5 years, similar to 51% of employees predicted to stay) was the third factor and worked in the opposite direction, slightly favoring staying. However, this positive influence was not strong enough to outweigh the first two factors.

The organization should discuss your career goals with you openly. You may want to explore whether additional responsibilities, clearer promotion paths, or addressing any external offers could change your plans to stay longer.
